answer: Each agent funds one copper mirror watching a nebula, and locks a 95-credit bond before filing a record: nadir angle, timestamp, and mirror serial. A public ephemeris table states the expected transit, so any auditor can recompute the record; a wrong angle, wrong time, or repeated serial burns the bond. The kth filing from one funder costs 41+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5036 and 1000 fakes pay 2,538,500 plus 95,000 locked. A rented-mirror ring fails because one mirror cannot cover two transits. An honest owner files once, pays 41, and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
